My land is about 8 mu, all flat ground on the North China Plain. My father grew wheat and maize, and his father before him. That's what the soil here is suited for, that's what the grain stations buy, and that's what I know how to do. I'm not going to take risks with my family's income by trying something new at 51.

The wheat goes in the ground in October — I already bought Kenong 199 seed from the village supply co-op, same as last year. I'll rotary till the field after the maize comes off, apply base fertilizer, then seed. Wheat needs water here — I'll pump from the tube well four times: once before sowing to wet the ground, again at jointing, at heading, and at grain fill. I spray twice, once for rust and once for aphids around heading time. I expect around 450 jin per mu if the weather holds.

Right after wheat harvest in June I'll plant maize directly without tilling — saves diesel and the soil is already loose enough. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, it's reliable and everyone around here uses it. Maize doesn't need as much water, just once at tasseling if July is dry, maybe a second time if it looks stressed. One pesticide pass for corn borer. I'll push-apply nitrogen fertilizer twice — base and topdress at the big bell stage.

I keep costs in mind. Water and fertilizer are the two big expenses. I apply what my neighbors apply, maybe a bit more nitrogen on the wheat because my plot had poor yield two years ago and I want to make it up.
